blurb: Plucky white Scottish terrier with a harsh coat and a rounded, fluffy face
description: The West Highland White Terrier is a small Scottish terrier with a harsh white double coat, prick ears and a confident, energetic and independent character.
answer: The West Highland White Terrier, or Westie, is a Scottish terrier bred to hunt small rodents. It stands about 25–28 cm and weighs around 7–9 kg, and is described as intelligent, self-assured and energetic, with a high prey drive.

body: White terriers were recorded in Scotland under James VI. Several white lines existed in the nineteenth century, including the Duke of Argyll's Roseneath Terrier and Dr Flaxman's Pittenweem Terrier. Edward Donald Malcolm, Laird of Poltalloch, is credited with the modern breed after one of his reddish terriers was reportedly mistaken for a fox and shot.

The name West Highland White Terrier first appeared in print in 1908. The first club formed in 1904, the Kennel Club recognised the breed in 1907, and it reached the United States around 1907–1908. Westies have won Best in Show at both Westminster and Crufts.

Westies typically weigh 6.8–9.1 kg and stand 25–28 cm, with a body shorter than their height. They have dark, almond-shaped eyes, pointed erect ears, a black nose, a deep chest and a short, sturdy tail. The harsh outer coat grows to about 5 cm over a soft, thick undercoat and fills out the face; it is hand-stripped or clipped. Most are pure white.

Westies are commonly described as intelligent, quick to learn, independent and confident, and as the most sociable of the Scottish terriers. Some are good with children, but they rarely tolerate rough handling and can be possessive of food and toys. They may be stubborn, and like to bark and dig.

Bred to hunt rodents on farms, the breed is energetic and is commonly said to need around an hour of exercise a day. Training from a young age is considered important, and the coat needs regular stripping or clipping.

Conditions reported in the breed include craniomandibular osteopathy, known as Westie jaw, atopic dermatitis, the breed-specific skin disease hyperplastic dermatosis, globoid cell leukodystrophy, white dog shaker syndrome, Legg–Calvé–Perthes disease and chronic hepatitis. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years.

faq.q: How big does a Westie get?
faq.a: Westies typically stand 25–28 cm at the withers and weigh about 6.8–9.1 kg.
Many are friendly with children, but they rarely tolerate rough handling such as ear or fur pulling, so supervision and early training are advised.

faq.q: How long do West Highland White Terriers live?
faq.a: A 2024 British study found a life expectancy of 13.4 years, and a 2015 French study found 12.93 years.
